agent_interface.operating_principle: The agent may organize visible facts and explain the next valid command. It must stop at permission, identity, policy, evidence, revision, access, or human-decision boundaries. Qualification, assignment, quote readiness, exception decisions, and handoff acknowledgement remain attributable human commands.

escalation_conditions: the requester disputes staff-visible facts
restricted information is requested
no permitted correction command is available
stop_conditions: request capability is missing or invalid

escalation_conditions: unsupported work requires owner authority
risk or service-area policy conflicts
clarification remains unresolved past its policy target
stop_conditions: identity or tenant scope is unresolved

escalation_conditions: the next action requires owner authority
evidence conflicts with requester-visible scope
privacy or safety facts restrict access
required_context: current request, qualification, assignment, evidence, visit, exception, readiness, and handoff refs
stop_conditions: more than one primary transition is simultaneously selected
a required entity version is missing
success_evidence: updated state on the active dossier seam

escalation_conditions: no eligible estimator can accept
the request is repeatedly returned
assignment closure needs owner authority
success_evidence: accountable estimator actor id when assigned

escalation_conditions: no access or unsafe conditions stop the visit
a material scope difference needs correction
owner authority is required to cancel or authorize rescheduling
stop_conditions: assigned estimator identity does not match

escalation_conditions: sensitive decision details need restriction
policy authority is unclear
the package remains not ready after its named correction
stop_conditions: the actor is not the acknowledged assigned estimator

escalation_conditions: the recipient rejects the package
access fails without an authorized alternative
material evidence or scope changes after transfer
stop_conditions: the readiness decision is not current and quote-ready

escalation_conditions: the target date passes without a decision
the exception reopens
privacy, safety, capacity, or service-policy facts conflict
stop_conditions: owner authority is absent for a decision

assertions: evidence rail and decision seam are visually distinct without relying on copy
no KPI strip or generic card grid appears
request identity and current state remain pinned
rail switcher preserves the active request
the primary action is reachable by keyboard and touch
blocked and error messages do not rely on color
field errors identify the field and correction
submission completion names the next human step
all checklist items and evidence links are keyboard reachable
ready and not-ready decisions require explicit confirmation
decision text and evidence remain readable at 200 percent zoom

forbidden_fallbacks: invented analytics or sample customer activity

silhouette_test.method: Hide the product name, logo, and customer copy on the primary request screen.
silhouette_test.passing_observation: The centered request spine, clipped evidence rail, stitched decision seam, and single bottom next-move dock still identify estimate-request qualification work rather than a generic dashboard.
rejection_conditions: a KPI strip becomes the main first-viewport object
the request is replaced by a generic card grid
evidence and decisions lose their visible attachment to the request
factory or implementation metadata appears as a customer panel

language_system.audience_description: Small residential service teams whose office coordinator, estimator, and owner need one accountable path from an incoming estimate request to a quote-ready handoff. Requesters see only their request, evidence, visit choices, and clear next step.

orientation_steps: Choose the request source and record the requester's contact, service location, requested work, and follow-up consent.
Review the request dossier for missing or contradictory facts.
Record clarification, supported work, or owner review as the one attributable next step.
first_run.promise: Turn one scattered estimate request into a visible, owned next step without replacing accounting or dispatch.
first_run.success_message: Request captured. The source and details are saved, and the next review belongs to {next_accountable_person}.

language_system.user_goal: Move each request from first contact to an assigned, evidence-backed quote-ready package while keeping every correction and decision attributable.

definitions.plain_language: The requester's contact, location, requested work, consent, source channel, and correction history.
A coordinator or authorized owner recorded that the request fits the current service rules. It is not a promise to perform the work.
A versioned photo, measurement, document, or note used in a named operational decision.
A scheduled field review that records attributable observations and access outcomes.
The assigned estimator recorded that the current checklist passed with usable evidence and no unresolved blocker. No quote has been issued by this state alone.
An immutable package version transferred to a verified recipient with its readiness decision, evidence refs, limits, and open obligations.
A blocker or authority question with an owner, target date, requested decision, and retained resolution evidence.

voice_principles: Name the request, the accountable person, and the next step in the first sentence.
Use the requester's words for the work. Keep policy and system vocabulary in staff-only supporting text.
State what is missing and how to correct it. Do not use vague failure copy.
Separate recorded facts from decisions and limits. Never turn quote-ready into a sales or revenue claim.
Use calm, direct sentences. Do not praise routine actions or imply urgency that no policy supports.

primary_task.objective: Open one incoming estimate request, complete its minimum facts, and record the accountable next step without losing its source or requester-visible history.
primary_task.success_signal: The request spine shows a retained source, complete minimum details, a current state, one accountable person, and one permission-valid next move backed by an executable command ref.

signature_components.interaction: Keep the original request, requester-visible corrections, source channel, and identity fixed in view while staff work through qualification, assignment, evidence, and readiness.
signature_components.name: Request spine

signature_components.interaction: Show versioned photos, measurements, notes, review status, disputes, and access restrictions beside the decision that cites them.
signature_components.name: Evidence rail

signature_components.interaction: Stitch qualification, assignment, exception, readiness, and handoff decisions into one chronological edge with actor, time, reason, evidence, and current validity.
signature_components.name: Decision seam

signature_components.interaction: Present one permission-valid primary command, explain its guard in plain language, and keep alternatives subordinate.
signature_components.name: Next-move dock

signature_components.interaction: Pair each readiness criterion with the exact evidence version, result, limitation, and responsible reviewer before a final decision command becomes available.
signature_components.name: Readiness stitch

anti_bloat_rules: Show one request and one primary next move at a time.
Keep history collapsed until the user asks for prior versions or decisions.
Put advanced policy, retention, archive, restore, restriction, and invalidation controls behind a named More actions disclosure.
Use queue rows for comparison and the dossier for action. Do not duplicate full forms inside cards.
Never display implementation metadata as a customer-facing panel.

save_behavior.status_feedback: Show Saving beside the edited section, then Saved with the latest revision. A command result must name the new state and accountable next step. A stale revision keeps the user's draft and asks them to review the changed facts before retrying.
